entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
World War I, also known as the Great War, was a global conflict that lasted from 1914 to 1918. It originated in Europe and involved many of the world's major powers.

This war was sparked by a complex system of alliances and conflicting national interests.

The war led to the rise of new global power structures and the redrawing of national borders.

The war had a profound impact on the world, leading to the Russian Revolution, the collapse of empires, and the eventual emergence of the United States as a global superpower.

The war also saw the introduction of new military technologies and tactics, including the use of tanks and poison gas.

The war resulted in an estimated 37 million casualties, including 17 million dead and 20 million wounded.

entities.summary: Global conflict centered in Europe from 1914 to 1918, triggered by the July Crisis following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand. The war involved over 30 nations, introduced industrialized warfare, and caused approximately 20 million deaths. It reshaped geopolitics, dissolved empires, and set the stage for World War II.
